question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Post-stimulus degron depletion
ideas.description: Prime cells with a transient stimulus, then acutely degrade FOS/JUN (dTAG/AID) after the stimulus ends and before re-challenge. If the faster or stronger secondary response is lost, AP-1 is needed to maintain memory and not only to establish it.

ideas.title: Chromatin state tracking through washout
ideas.description: Run CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN and ATAC-seq plus H3K27ac at several times after stimulus removal. Compare how long AP-1 occupancy, accessibility and marks persist, and whether accessibility outlasts AP-1 binding, which would indicate AP-1 acts as an initiator and not a maintainer.

ideas.title: Single-cell hysteresis imaging
ideas.description: Image an endogenous FOS or AP-1 reporter in single cells through repeated stimulus pulses with variable intervals. Look for history-dependent responses and heritable states across divisions, and link them to later transcription by lineage tracking.

ideas.title: Motif-specific enhancer editing
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base or prime editing to mutate AP-1 motifs at selected primed enhancers, then compare the secondary response with unedited controls. This tests whether AP-1 binding at those specific sites is required for the memory at the associated genes.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 recruitment sufficiency test
ideas.description: Use dCas9 to recruit AP-1 or a pioneer-like FOS/JUN domain to a neutral reporter locus with a transient pulse. Then test whether the locus keeps a more accessible state and responds faster after the recruitment is gone, which would show AP-1 is sufficient for memory.

candidates: ChIP/CUT&RUN of FOS/JUN before, during, and after transient stimulus to see persistent occupancy
ATAC-seq time course after stimulus withdrawal to track lasting accessibility at AP-1 motifs
Acute degron (dTAG/AID) depletion of FOS/JUN after stimulus to test if AP-1 is needed for maintaining memory vs. establishing it
Optogenetic pulsed AP-1 activation with varied timing to test priming/memory of prior dosing
Single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) lineage-tracing of memory of prior stimulus across divisions
Live imaging of AP-1 reporter (FOS-GFP) in single cells across repeated stimuli to measure hysteresis
Dominant-negative A-FOS expression timed after priming to erase memory
Mutating AP-1 motifs at specific enhancers by CRISPR to test necessity for faster secondary response
dCas9-based synthetic recruitment of AP-1 to a neutral locus to test sufficiency for creating memory
Histone mark profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) at AP-1 sites after stimulus decay
Hi-C/Micro-C to test whether AP-1 maintains loops after stimulus
Pioneer activity assay: nucleosome positioning with MNase at AP-1 sites in primed vs naive cells
Mathematical modeling of AP-1 feedback (FOS/JUN autoregulation) to predict bistability and compare with data
Mitotic bookmarking assay: live-cell imaging and CUT&RUN of AP-1 on mitotic chromosomes
Compare AP-1 memory across cell types (fibroblast, macrophage, neuron) with same stimulus
Proteomics of AP-1 dimer composition shifts (FOS vs. FOSL vs. ATF) after priming
Phosphorylation/post-translational state of JUN (JNK) persistence measurement
Cell-cycle-synchronized priming to test replication-dependence of memory
In vivo wound/inflammation re-challenge in AP-1 conditional knockout mice
Perturb-seq of AP-1 family members to map which paralogs affect memory of response
Measure memory decay half-life vs. AP-1 level via titration
Single-molecule tracking of JUN residence time at primed vs naive loci
